newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom seen worth up to $30 billion.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom seen worth up to $30 billion.

text.p: France Telecom, due to be partially privatised next month, is worth between 150 billion and 180 billion francs ($30 billion), according to analysts' first public estimates released on Monday.
Many Paris-based analysts declined to release their predictions for fear of upsetting the Finance Ministry in what could be France's biggest privatisation.
There was no immediate comment from banks Paribas and BNP , who are coordinating the placement and were collecting analysts' figures.
ABN Amro Hoare Govett analyst James Downie put a value of 150 billion to 180 billion francs on France Telecom SA .

According to a document obtained by Reuters, Downie said that at the top end of the range France Telecom "will still be inexpensively priced, valued in Price/Earnings terms (at 12.8 times 1997 earnings)".
Market sources said other analysts were in the same range of 150 billion and higher but there was no official confirmation.

"We expect France Telecom's normalised net earnings to grow at around 11 percent per year over the next five years. This figure has been adjusted to strip out one-off accounting changes in 1996," the AMRO document said.

"The company is strongly cash generative, and should be able to pay down debt from 107 billion francs in 1996 to 50 billion francs in 2001, reducing gearing from 136 percent to 41 percent in the process," he added.
A value of 150 billion to 180 billion francs would mean a share price of between 150 and 180 francs.
Fund managers reported that a number of banks were contacting them with analysts' estimates, but many banks and brokers declined to comment to journalists.
Under the placement rules, analysts are free to publish their value estimates this week following a March 20 briefing by the company.

BZW in June 1996 published a document which roughly valued France Telecom at between 150 billion and 200 billion francs. Fund managers said BZW was now "more towards 150 billion than 200 billion". BZW declined to comment.
The Finance Ministry will on May 5 announce a price range for France Telecom after which there will be a three week reservation period for private investors.
On May 26 the final price will be set and the Initial Public Offering will take place between May 27 and June 3.
The French government aims to raise between 30 billion and 50 billion francs from the sale of a minority stake in France Telecom.
France Telecom chairman Michel Bon said on March 28 the sale would involve a stake of between 30 and 40 percent of the company's capital.
